_comment: Mutations that survive with an argument for why no test can tell the difference. A blank reason fails the run - see verdict() in scripts/check-guard-mutations.py. Verify each claim before adding one; an unverified entry is how a survivor list becomes a formality. Note that the object-literal form `block: true,` is NEVER equivalent - Pi reads the field - and belongs in a test, not here. Keys carry LINE NUMBERS and therefore expire: inserting code above an entry moves its site, the entry stops matching, and the survivor reappears looking new. That happened on 2026-08-10 to phase-gate.ts:287:38. When a survivor you recognise comes back, check whether an existing entry just moved before writing a second one.
bash-containment.ts:47:10:true->false: Type declaration, not code: `export interface ContainmentBlock { block: true; }`. TypeScript types are erased before the module runs, so the mutant is byte-identical at runtime and no test can distinguish it. Verified by reading lines 46-49.
loop-detect.ts:44:10:true->false: Same shape as bash-containment.ts:47 - `block: true;` inside an interface declaration, erased at runtime. Note the semicolon: the object-literal form ends in a comma and IS a real hole, which is why loop-detect.ts:73 is a test and not an entry here.
queue-advancer.ts:81:12:true->false: `paused?: true;` - an optional property in a type declaration. The `?:` syntax exists only in types, so this cannot reach runtime.
task-queue-guard.ts:106:10:true->false: `export interface QueueBlock { block: true; }` - a type declaration, erased at runtime. Verified by reading lines 104-108. The two object-literal sites in this file (the tool-first refusal and the Section 1 dual-track refusal) are covered by tests asserting the field, not by entries here.
queue-advancer.ts:151:36:||->&&: `if (typeof queueDir !== "string" || !queueDir) return null;` with && lets an empty string through, and the very next statement calls currentTask(queueDir) inside a try/catch that returns null on any throw. An empty path throws there, so both versions return null for every input - the observable behaviour is identical and no test can separate them. Verified by reading lines 150-158.
approval.ts:71:13:||->&&: `if (!text || text.length > MAX) return false;` with && lets an empty string through, and an empty string then matches neither approval pattern, so it returns false by the other door. Identical observable behaviour for every input - same shape as queue-advancer.ts:151. Verified by reading isHumanApproval end to end.
phase-notice.ts:90:16:||->&&: `if (!queue || !existsSync(queue)) return null;` with && lets a nonexistent queue path through, and the loop below then compares dirname(dirname(status.txt)) against it, which cannot match for a path that is not there. Both versions return null for every input. Same shape as queue-advancer.ts:151 and approval.ts:71. Verified by reading afterToolResult end to end.
phase-notice.ts:43:34:&&->||: `typeof p === "string" && p` with || lets a non-string path reach resolve(), which throws TypeError for a number, object or array, and the surrounding try/catch turns that into `continue`. Every input reaches the same answer by a different route, so no test can separate them. Verified by reading writeTargets and the resolve() try/catch together.
phase-gate.ts:104:10:true->false: `export interface PhaseBlock { block: true; }` — a type declaration, erased before the module runs, so the mutant is byte-identical at runtime. Same shape as the entries for bash-containment.ts:47 and task-queue-guard.ts:106. Verified by reading lines 103-106.
phase-gate.ts:152:36:||->&&: `if (typeof queueDir !== "string" || !queueDir || !existsSync(queueDir)) return "open";` in phaseOf. With && a non-string truthy value passes the first clause, and every route below it fails open anyway: readdirSync throws inside tasks(), which catches and returns [], and `if (!all.length) return "open"` gives the same answer by the other door. Verified empirically — the mutant returns "open" for undefined, null, 5, {} and [] exactly as the original does, and tests/test_phase_tool_gate.py::TestFailsOpenOnWhatItCannotRecognise asserts those five.
phase-gate.ts:152:49:||->&&: Same clause as 152:36, the second `||`. With && an empty or missing path reaches tasks(), whose readdirSync throws into its own catch and returns [], and phaseOf then returns "open" from `if (!all.length)`. Same observable answer for every input, reached one line later. Verified against "" and "/definitely/missing/queue", both covered by TestFailsOpenOnWhatItCannotRecognise.
phase-gate.ts:330:38:||->&&: `if (typeof queueDir !== "string" || !queueDir) return null;` at the top of check(). With && a non-string truthy value continues instead of returning, and the very next statement calls phaseOf(queueDir), which fails open to "open", and `if (phase === "open") return null` returns the same null. The isolated clause is NOT equivalent; the function is, because the guard below it catches the same inputs. Verified for null, 5, {} and [] in TestFailsOpenOnWhatItCannotRecognise, which asserts check() returns null for each. NOTE: this entry was keyed 287:38 until 2026-08-10, when code inserted above it moved the line and the entry silently stopped matching — the survivor reappeared as if it were new. Allowlist keys carry line numbers and therefore expire whenever a file grows above them; re-verify rather than re-argue when one shows up again.
phase-gate.ts:209:12:false->true: Defensive `return false` on a path that cannot be reached: `resolve()` throws only for a non-string, and both arguments here are strings by the time they arrive — `queueDir` is type-checked at the top of check(), and the targets come from writeTargets(), which only ever returns strings. Flipping it to `true` would make the gate yield on every call, which every refusal test would catch — so the fact that none do is itself the evidence that the branch never executes. Verified by reading allWritesEscapeProject end to end.
phase-gate.ts:217:14:false->true: Defensive `return false` on a path that cannot be reached: `resolve()` throws only for a non-string, and both arguments here are strings by the time they arrive — the target is a string from writeTargets() and queueDir is type-checked at the top of check(). Flipping it to `true` would make the gate yield on every call, which every refusal test would catch — so the fact that none do is itself the evidence that the branch never executes. Verified by reading allWritesEscapeProject end to end.
phase-gate.ts:211:21:false->true: `if (!root) return false;` where root is the result of `resolve()`, which never returns an empty string for any input that did not throw — the throwing case is handled by the catch above. The clause is a belt on braces; flipping it changes behaviour only for a value that cannot occur. Verified by reading the two lines together.
bash-containment.ts:297:17:||->&&: `if (!tokens || tokens.length < 2) continue;` inside writeTargets. With && a null `tokens` reaches `tokens.length` and throws, and every caller wraps writeTargets in a try/catch that fails open — the same answer the original reaches by continuing. Probed 2026-08-10 against ten odd inputs (empty, bare operators, unbalanced quotes): the regex `match` returns null only for input the loop then skips anyway, so the throwing branch is unreachable in practice and no test can separate the two.
bash-containment.ts:335:30:||->&&: `isAbsolute(target) || /^[A-Za-z]:[\/]/.test(target)` in escapesCwd. With && a POSIX-absolute path like `/tmp/x` takes the `resolve(cwd, target)` branch instead of `resolve(target)`, and `isScratch` is called with BOTH the resolved path and the raw token precisely so that case still reads as scratch — the raw `/tmp/` prefix matches either way. Windows drive paths satisfy both operands, so they are unaffected. Same observable answer for every input the guard sees.
bash-containment.ts:339:12:false->true: `return false` in escapesCwd's catch, taken only when `resolve()` throws. `resolve` throws for a non-string, and every target reaching it came from writeTargets, which returns strings only. Flipping it to `true` would make an unparsable target read as escaping and refuse the call — a fail-CLOSED change that every ordinary-work test would catch, so the fact that none do is the evidence that the branch never runs.
bash-containment.ts:265:35:||->&&: `if (typeof command !== "string" || !command.trim()) return [];` at the top of writeTargets. With && an empty or whitespace-only string continues instead of returning early, and every extractor below finds nothing in it — the regexes match no operator and `seg.trim().match(...)` returns null for each segment, so the function returns [] from the bottom instead of the top. Verified by calling writeTargets on "", " ", "|", ";;" and "&&": every one yields [] in both versions. Same shape as the entries for queue-advancer.ts:151 and approval.ts:71.
bash-containment.ts:358:31:||->&&: `if (typeof cwd !== "string" || !cwd) return null;` at the top of bashContainmentBlock. With && an empty-string cwd continues, and `escapesCwd` then returns false for every target because its own `if (!target || !cwd) return false` catches it — null by the other door. Probed 2026-08-10 with cwd undefined/null/5/{}/"": the mutant returns null for all five, exactly as the original does. Same shape as phase-gate.ts:330:38. NOTE: keyed 354:31 for about ten minutes on 2026-08-10 before four comment lines added above it moved the site — the second line-number expiry in one session. The keying scheme is the defect; until it changes, expect a familiar survivor to be a moved entry.
goal-restate.ts:114:18:0->1: Field initializer on `private acts = 0;` (and `sent` on the next line), not the assignment that matters. Every path that reads either counter runs through `begin()` first, which sets both to 0 unconditionally, and `afterToolResult` returns on a null goal before reading them — `goal` is null until `begin()` is called, so no caller can observe the initial value. The assignments inside `begin()` ARE observable and are covered: test_new_cycle_gives_the_full_run_up pins the acts reset and test_new_cycle_restores_the_budget pins the sent reset. Verified by reading GoalRestate end to end. NOTE: re-keyed 2026-08-10 after the file grew. The moved-entry matcher could not resolve these automatically because TWO entries share the same column and operator (acts and sent), and an ambiguous match fails loudly rather than guessing — which is the correct behaviour and the reason a hand re-key was still needed.
